quizzes.title: Event details of National Panchayati Raj Day
quizzes.passage: National Panchayati Raj Day is an occasion to reflect on local self-government in India. The day marks the enforcement of a constitutional amendment that was aimed at strengthening grassroots democracy and decentralised governance. The bill for this amendment was introduced in the Lok Sabha in September 1991, when a Congress government was in office. The amendment is described as having several important effects. Inclusive development ensures the participation of marginalised groups in local decisions. Localised planning promotes need-based development in villages and districts. Digital transformation is also listed among its significant effects. The amendment added a new Part to the Constitution, titled The Panchayats, and a new schedule that lists subjects for panchayats. It provides for a three-tier structure of panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels. The amendment also provides that a state with a population not exceeding twenty lakh may skip the intermediate level of panchayats. It also provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Madhya Pradesh was the first state to implement the amendment. The amendment's provisions are set out in Articles 243 to 243-O of the Constitution. Its provisions also deal with the term of panchayats, their finances and the conduct of their elections. Panchayats are the basic units through which these goals are pursued.

questions.q: Which ministry organised the 17th National Panchayati Raj Day?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the day was organised by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj.

questions.q: Which index measures grassroots development and tracks panchayat performance?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0 as measuring grassroots development and tracking panchayat performance.

questions.q: What is e-GramSwaraj used for, according to the booklet?
questions.explanation: The booklet says e-GramSwaraj is used for transparent monitoring and data-driven governance.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The National Panchayat Awards recognise best-performing panchayats.
Reason (R): Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0 measures grassroots development and tracks panchayat performance.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the Index is a separate initiative and does not explain the Awards.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. National Panchayat Awards   ->   A. Transparent monitoring and data-driven governance
II. Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0   ->   B. Recognises best-performing panchayats
III. e-GramSwaraj   ->   C. Measures grassroots development and tracks panchayat performance
IV. Theme of the 17th National Panchayati Raj Day   ->   D. Sashakt Panchayat, Sarvangeen Vikas
questions.explanation: Each award, index, portal and theme matches the description the booklet gives for it.

questions.q:
Read the statements about the 17th National Panchayati Raj Day:
I. The event was held at Vigyan Bhawan.
II. e-GramSwaraj is used for transparent monitoring and data-driven governance.
III. The theme of the day was 'Gram Swaraj, Viksit Bharat'.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because the booklet gives the theme as Sashakt Panchayat, Sarvangeen Vikas.

questions.q:
Examine the statements below about the 17th National Panchayati Raj Day.
I. The event was observed in 2026.
II. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj organised the day.
III. The theme of the day was 'Viksit Panchayat, Samriddh Bharat'.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while statement III names a theme the booklet does not give.

quizzes.title: Elections, reservation and oversight in panchayats
quizzes.passage: Panchayati Raj institutions are the system of local self-government that the amendment established in rural areas. The amendment added a new Part to the Constitution, titled The Panchayats, and its provisions are set out in Articles 243 to 243-O. Under this framework, panchayats function at three levels, namely the village, intermediate and district levels. The framework also provides for reservation of seats for women, so that women hold a set share of seats and offices in panchayats at each level. A panchayat can be dissolved before it completes its period, and when this happens fresh elections are needed to constitute a new panchayat. Such elections must be completed within a set period, and where the remaining period is short, an election need not be held. The amendment also added an 11th Schedule that lists subjects for panchayats. The bill for it was introduced in the Lok Sabha in September 1991 under a Congress government. The amendment's significance is described in three heads: inclusive development, which ensures the participation of marginalised groups; localised planning, which promotes need-based development; and digital transformation. Madhya Pradesh was the first state to implement the amendment. The framework was built to strengthen grassroots democracy and decentralised governance.

questions.q: Not less than what share of the total seats in panchayats is reserved for women?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that not less than one-third of total seats and chairperson offices are reserved for women.

questions.q: Within what period after a panchayat is dissolved must fresh elections be completed?
questions.explanation: Fresh elections must be completed before six months from the date of dissolution expire.

questions.q: The chairperson of a panchayat at which level is elected in the manner the State Legislature determines?
questions.explanation: The village-level chairperson is elected in the manner the State Legislature determines.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Chairpersons at the intermediate and district levels of panchayats are elected indirectly.
Reason (R): They are elected by and from amongst the elected members.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: R states the method of indirect election, which is exactly what A describes.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. State Election Commission   ->   A. Reviews panchayat finances
II. Finance Commission   ->   B. Supervises electoral rolls and the conduct of panchayat elections
III. Seat reservation for Scheduled Castes   ->   C. Not applicable in Arunachal Pradesh
IV. Duration of a panchayat   ->   D. Five years, unless dissolved earlier
questions.explanation: The State Election Commission supervises elections, the Finance Commission reviews finances, and the SC reservation provision does not apply in Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.q:
Read the statements about panchayat elections and reservation:
I. All members of panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels are elected directly.
II. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population.
III. Chairpersons at the intermediate level are appointed by the State Government.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because intermediate-level chairpersons are elected indirectly by the elected members.

questions.q:
Examine the statements below about panchayat reservation and terms.
I. Not less than one-third of seats are reserved for women.
II. Reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes is not applicable to Arunachal Pradesh.
III. Fresh elections may be held up to twelve months after dissolution.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are in the booklet, while III contradicts the six-month limit for fresh elections.

questions.q: After how many years does the Governor constitute a Finance Commission to review panchayat finances? (number of years)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Governor constitutes a Finance Commission after every five years.

questions.q: Within how many months of a panchayat's dissolution must fresh elections be completed? (number of months)
questions.explanation: Fresh elections must be completed before six months from the dissolution expire.

questions.q: Which body supervises the electoral rolls and the conduct of panchayat elections? (name)
questions.explanation: The State Election Commission has superintendence, direction and control of panchayat elections.

questions.q: For which state is reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes in panchayats not applicable? (name of state)
questions.explanation: The booklet notes that the SC seat reservation provision is not applicable to Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.q: Which body determines the manner of electing the village-level chairperson? (name)
questions.explanation: The village-level chairperson is elected in the manner the State Legislature determines.

questions.q: What is the minimum share of total seats reserved for women in panchayats? (fraction)
questions.explanation: Not less than one-third of total seats are reserved for women.

questions.q: Under which Article are all members of panchayats at each level elected directly? (Article number)
questions.explanation: Article 243-C provides that all members of panchayats at the village, intermediate and district levels are elected directly.

quizzes.title: Exemptions, Union Territories and PESA
quizzes.passage: The Constitution's panchayat provisions do not apply uniformly to every part of India. Certain states and areas are exempted from the framework, and the amendment's rules set out these exemptions directly. These exemptions cover some states as well as some areas within other states. The framework was added as a new Part titled The Panchayats, consisting of provisions from Articles 243 to 243-O. Its provisions give panchayats a three-tier structure at the village, intermediate and district levels, and they provide for elections and for reservation of seats. The amendment also provides that a state with a population not exceeding twenty lakh may skip the intermediate level of panchayats. The amendment's significance is described under three heads: inclusive development, localised planning and digital transformation. The amendment also added an 11th Schedule that lists subjects for panchayats. Madhya Pradesh was the first state to implement it, and the bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in September 1991 under a Congress government. Its provisions also deal with the duration of panchayats and their finances. The provisions are meant to strengthen grassroots democracy and decentralised governance. Each of these features forms part of the framework described above.

questions.q: Which Union Territory is excluded from the application of the panchayat provisions?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the provisions apply to all Union Territories except Delhi.

questions.q: Which Act, enacted under Article 243-M, is popularly known as the PESA Act?
options: Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996
questions.explanation: The Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 is popularly called the PESA Act.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed in the booklet as a Sixth Schedule state?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram as the Sixth Schedule states.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The PESA Act, 1996 does not apply to Sixth Schedule areas.
Reason (R): The PESA Act, 1996 was enacted under Article 243-M.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are in the booklet, but the article under which PESA was enacted does not explain why it excludes Sixth Schedule areas.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Article 243-L   ->   A. Enables the President to extend Part IX to Union Territories
II. PESA Act, 1996   ->   B. Enacted under Article 243-M
III. Darjeeling district   ->   C. Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council exists there
IV. Hill Areas of Manipur   ->   D. District Councils exist there
questions.explanation: Article 243-L covers extension to Union Territories, PESA was enacted under Article 243-M, and the Darjeeling and Manipur items are tied to their councils.

questions.q:
Read the statements about the exemptions and the framework:
I. Part IX applies to Union Territories subject to exceptions the President may specify.
II. Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram are exempted from the provisions.
III. The PESA Act, 1996 was enacted under Article 243-L.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement III is wrong because the PESA Act was enacted under Article 243-M, not 243-L.

questions.q:
Examine the statements below about exemptions.
I. Scheduled Areas in Fifth and Sixth Schedule states are exempted.
II. Darjeeling district is exempted because the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council exists.
III. Assam is not a Sixth Schedule state.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while statement III contradicts the booklet's list of Sixth Schedule states.

questions.q: Under which Article may the President direct that the panchayat provisions apply to a Union Territory? (Article number)
questions.explanation: Article 243-L lets the President direct application to Union Territories, subject to exceptions and modifications.

questions.q: Under which Article was the PESA Act enacted? (Article number)
questions.explanation: The PESA Act, 1996 was enacted under Article 243-M.

questions.q: In which year was the Act popularly known as PESA enacted? (year)
questions.explanation: The full name of the PESA Act carries the year 1996.

questions.q: How many states are listed in the booklet as Sixth Schedule states? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram as the Sixth Schedule states.

questions.q: Which district of West Bengal is exempted because the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council exists? (name of district)
questions.explanation: The Darjeeling district of West Bengal is exempted where the Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council exists.

questions.q: In which state are the Hill Areas exempted where District Councils exist? (name of state)
questions.explanation: The Hill Areas of Manipur for which District Councils exist are exempted.

questions.q: Apart from Nagaland and Mizoram, which state is named among the states exempted from the framework? (name of state)
questions.explanation: Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram are the exempted states named in the booklet.
